selected_problem: Fresh main could verify a PR-create response against expectedHeadSha when one was supplied, but gitRemoteDelivery still allowed `createPullRequest=true` with `push=false` and no expected head. That path could create an externally visible PR without any validated-commit binding, bypassing the new receipt integrity contract.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: The fresh main left a singular deterministic bypass around the newly-established PR head binding: remote delivery did not require the binding value before PR creation. The evidence-rich central bottleneck routes to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced rotation.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt or fabricated numeric routing score is claimed.

pre_fix_reproduction.observation: Calling gitRemoteDelivery with explicitApproval=true, push=false, createPullRequest=true and no expectedHeadSha reached githubCreatePullRequest and could perform the GitHub POST because the helper treated head binding as optional.
pre_fix_reproduction.consequence: The provider-level remote delivery contract could create a PR with no validated commit identity even though push and merge paths already required expected-head binding.

changes: gitRemoteDelivery now requires a non-empty expectedHeadSha whenever push, PR creation, or merge is requested.
The gate runs immediately after explicit-approval verification and before any push or GitHub API side effect.
No-op remote-delivery calls with no external operation requested remain unaffected.
Existing lower-level push/merge validation remains in place for malformed or unresolved expected commits.

commands: node --test exact candidate PR receipt + PR head + remote hard-gate focused tests
cases: remote PR creation without expected head fails before fetch/GitHub side effect
remote PR creation with expected head and matching returned PR head succeeds
previous PR create head-integrity 3/3 regressions remain passing
previous PR create receipt-integrity 2/2 regressions remain passing
validation.verification_note: The candidate core/test files executed locally and their Git blob hashes match the branch content. No GitHub Actions were used.

truth_boundaries: This removes an unbound provider path but does not make GitHub PR creation atomically conditional on remote head identity; a branch can still move before the POST and produce a mismatched PR side effect, which the post-create head check detects and rejects.
The GitHub merge endpoint still lacks a caller-supplied expected-base-SHA precondition, so base movement remains unresolved.
OS-level validation sandboxing, arbitrary complex semantic synthesis, Windows descendant-tree equivalence, and crash-level filesystem atomicity remain unresolved.
No force push, repository-rule bypass, credential exposure, payment, formal Release, or destructive/irreversible external action is introduced.
